solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ring road charge

definitions.meaning: to ring a bell slowly and steadily, as for a funeral
a fee paid to use a road, bridge or tunnel

explanation.surface: A ring road that motorists must pay to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a bell's slow ringing and a fee for passage along a road.

clue.text: Tiny plant: cat's sat on leaf

indicators.note: in a down answer, sitting on something means coming above it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to leaf through a book is to thumb through it

explanation.surface: A tiny plant's leaf crushed because a cat has sat on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb 'leaf', as in leafing through pages, gives THUMB.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the folk-tale midget is a general horticultural term for a dwarf variety of plant.

clue.text: Odd for Scots to appear in genealogical list for French duchy

indicators.note: to appear in means to be placed inside, so the Scots word goes inside the list

parts.note: a line is a family's line of descent
orra is a Scottish word meaning odd or occasional

explanation.surface: Something odd for Scotsmen turning up in a family tree of French nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic duchy in north-east France, now a region bordering Germany.

clue.text: One has opus composed for this?

definitions.text: One has opus composed for this?

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical work written specially for a particular instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' signals an anagram of ONE HAS OPUS, and the whole clue doubles as the definition: a piece might well be written for this brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brass tuba-like instrument wrapped around the player, for which a musical piece could be composed.

clue.text: Possessor of tranquillisers uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its cover, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: downers is slang for depressant drugs such as tranquillisers

explanation.surface: The owner of a stash of tranquillisers has been exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: whoever possesses something holds title to it.

clue.text: Lively cunning grabs power completely

indicators.note: grabs means seizes and holds, so the word for cunning surrounds the rest

parts.note: sly means cunning
P is the physics symbol for power
right as in right through, meaning completely

explanation.surface: A lively, crafty person seizes power entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: spry, energetic, full of life.

clue.text: Treated pinker sore, upset with burn — this one revolted

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged
upset means turned over, so in a down answer the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: raw means sore, as of skin
burn and beck are both northern British words for a stream

explanation.surface: A medical scene: a pinker, sore burn is treated and the patient is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' rearranges PINKER; 'upset' turns RAW into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender to the English throne who led a rebellion against Henry VII in the 1490s.

clue.text: Severe test — exam without notes

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the exam word goes around the notes

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
D and E are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A tough oral exam taken without any notes to rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a painful trial or testing experience.

clue.text: Regularly take slices in because I hear more like a piece of cake

definitions.text: more like a piece of cake

indicators.note: taking regular slices from the words means picking every second letter of them

explanation.surface: Someone takes regular slices of cake, having heard it is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'because I hear' looks like a homophone signal but is the fodder; its even letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is idiom for something simple, so more like one means less difficult.

clue.text: Fever's odd, being brought about by a shower?

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the word for odd is read backwards

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: A strange fever that seems to be caused by getting caught in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' looks like 'caused', but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An old general term for infectious diseases of cattle, including feverish plagues.

clue.text: A yogurt phobia — oddly only a live one can produce this?

definitions.text: only a live one can produce this

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fear of yogurt, which seems a strange thing to write about.
explanation.definitionFit: A life story written by its own subject requires the author to be alive.

clue.text: Notes saint in screen in church

parts.note: three notes of the sol-fa scale: re, re and do

explanation.surface: Musical notes and a saint depicted on a screen inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental screen or panel behind the altar of a church.

clue.text: Listen all the way to the end of America's good cover

parts.note: to hear is to listen

parts.words: all the way to the end of America's
parts.note: thru is the American spelling of through, meaning all the way to the end

explanation.surface: Someone hears an American good all the way to its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's' tells you to use the US spelling THRU rather than THROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug laid before a fireplace is a covering for the floor there; vague but accurate.

clue.text: Angry, withholding page from copyright infringer

indicators.note: withholding means keeping something back, so the page letter is dropped

parts.note: a pirate copies books or music without permission

explanation.surface: An author is angry with someone pirating their work who holds back a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: furious, cross, incensed.

clue.text: Socialite's wordplay for NAMELY?

indicators.note: wordplay for says the answer is a set of instructions that would build the word in capitals

parts.note: the letters man turned about give NAM, and a town (Ely, in Cambridgeshire) gives ELY, together spelling this word

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking what wordplay would produce the word NAMELY.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as instructions. ELY is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashionable man who frequents parties and clubs is a classic socialite.

clue.text: Ignorant hunk now in gaol has this?

indicators.note: has means contains, so the clue words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A dim muscleman behind bars, ignorant of his situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: unaware, without knowledge.

clue.text: Tormented soul none set free

indicators.note: tormented means twisted or tortured, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tortured soul, finally released by nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen or release, so to free something tied up.

clue.text: Seeking to support small railway operation

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting underneath, so the seeking word comes below

parts.note: hunting means seeking

explanation.surface: Looking for a job supporting a small railway business.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving trains or wagons from one track to another in a siding is a routine rail task.

clue.text: Tool girl's holding right after drill, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the girl's piece behind the primate

parts.note: a drill is a kind of baboon, an example of a monkey

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the letter for right goes inside the word for girl

parts.note: wench is an old word for a girl

explanation.surface: A workshop scene: a girl holds the right tool after using a drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' wants to be a power tool, but it is the West African baboon.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustable spanner, a common tool for gripping nuts and pipes.

clue.text: Hotel's out of the base maybe for a sidecar — fruit syrup

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so the hotel letter is dropped

parts.words: the base maybe for a sidecar
parts.note: a chassis is the base frame of a vehicle, such as a motorcycle sidecar
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sidecar cocktail made with fruit syrup instead of a hotel's base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sidecar' tempts as the cocktail, but here it is the motorcycle attachment.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackcurrant liqueur or syrup from France, used in kir.

clue.text: Fruit mum used in toto

indicators.note: used in means put into, so the mother word goes inside the Latin word

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum uses the whole of the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in toto' is Latin for entirely, but here 'in' joins 'used' and toto is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a fruit, though usually eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Lover of loud noise sacrificing little volume

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving up, so the letters for a small volume are dropped

parts.note: a clamour is a loud, confused noise
CL is the abbreviation for centilitre, a small volume

explanation.surface: Someone fond of loud noise is giving up a little volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word can mean a beloved person, a sweetheart, as well as a love affair.

clue.text: Helpless over everything still in the seed drill?

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

parts.words: everything still in the seed drill
parts.note: if every seed is still in the machine, none has been sown

explanation.surface: A farmer is stuck with every seed still in the drill.
explanation.walkthrough: The seed drill here is a farm machine that plants seeds in rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone means having nobody to help, hence without assistance.

clue.text: Mineral containing chestnut pigment

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the horse letters go into the mineral

parts.note: an ore is a mineral from which metal is extracted
CH is the abbreviation for chestnut, a horse's colour

explanation.surface: A mineral containing a chestnut-coloured pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy yellow-brown pigment used by painters since prehistoric times.

clue.text: Dog — almost more intelligent one

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: sharper means quicker-witted, more intelligent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dog that is almost the brighter one of two.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese breed with a deeply wrinkled skin is a type of canine.

clue.text: Japanese who drew fish around America

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the fish is placed on either side of the country

parts.note: the hoki is a New Zealand food fish
USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A Japanese artist who sketched fish swimming around America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edo-period artist famous for The Great Wave off Kanagawa was a Japanese draughtsman and printmaker.

clue.text: Bird with varied grey tones around wing's leading edge

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go either side of one letter
varied means changed, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
the leading edge of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird with grey tones of different shades around the front edge of its wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grey tones' reads as plumage description, but 'varied' makes it anagram fodder, and 'leading edge' picks only the first letter of 'wing's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small white American heron, a species of bird.

clue.text: Pieces turned for joiner

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word for pieces is read backwards

parts.note: pieces is slang for guns

explanation.surface: Bits of wood turned on a lathe for a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a general carpenter but is one character: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snug the joiner is one of the Mechanicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare names one of his Mechanicals with a trade: this one is a carpenter who plays the Lion.
